    How It Works

    The Context Engineering Layer
    for AI Coding.

    lean-ctx is a compression system with three independent layers. A context server replaces your AI's file reads with AST-aware compressed versions. A shell hook intercepts 90+ CLI command patterns. And three communication protocols teach the AI to respond more efficiently. You install it once — everything else is automatic.

    The data flow

    Where does lean-ctx sit?

    lean-ctx intercepts at two levels: the context layer (file reads, code search, shell commands) and the shell layer (raw CLI output). Both compress data before it reaches the LLM. The AI sees the same information in a fraction of the tokens.

    data flow — before vs. after 
    Without lean-ctx:

You  →  AI Tool  →  reads file  (full content)  →  LLM processes everything

With lean-ctx:

You  →  AI Tool  →  lean-ctx compresses  →  signal only  →  LLM: 60–99% less noise
                           ├─ PathJail sandbox + size caps
                           ├─ AST-aware compression
                           ├─ Memory Runtime (knowledge + forgetting)
                           ├─ Session cache (re-read ≈ 13 tok)
                           └─ 10 read modes per file type

    You

    Code normally. Change nothing about your workflow.

    AI Tool

    Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, Windsurf, …

    lean-ctx

    Compresses everything via Context Server & Shell Hook.

    LLM

    Sees only signal. 60–90% fewer tokens, same information.

    Two commands. That's it.

    Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) Cache Eviction

    When the session cache is full, lean-ctx uses Reciprocal Rank Fusion to decide which entries to evict. Each signal (recency, frequency, size) is ranked independently, then fused into a single score — no arbitrary weight tuning required.

    Formula: RRF(d) = Σ 1/(K + rank_i(d)) where K=60. This handles signal incomparability (seconds vs counts vs tokens) without needing tuned weights, unlike traditional weighted combinations.

    Three compression layers

    How it actually works

    Three independent layers, each compressing data differently. All automatic. All transparent.

    Layer 1

    Context Server

    49 intelligent tools that replace your AI's built-in file reads, shell commands, and code searches with AST-aware compressed versions. 10 read modes adapt to every use case.

    ctx_read ctx_shell ctx_search +46
    Explore all tools
    Layer 2

    Shell Hook

    Intercepts shell output via aliases and recognizes 90+ command patterns — git, npm, cargo, docker, kubectl — compressing output at the terminal level.

    git npm cargo +87
    See all patterns
    Layer 3

    Protocols

    Instruction sets applied via system prompt that teach the AI to communicate more efficiently — act first, report concisely, use symbols instead of prose.

    Beyond pattern matching

    Scientific compression under the hood

    lean-ctx doesn't just strip whitespace — it uses six research-backed algorithms to decide what to keep and what to discard. Each algorithm targets a different dimension of information density.

    Predictive Surprise

    BPE cross-entropy scoring — keeps tokens that surprise a language model, discards predictable boilerplate.

    Spectral Relevance

    PageRank + heat diffusion on the dependency graph — propagates importance through code relationships.

    Boltzmann Allocation

    Statistical mechanics for token budgets — distributes context capacity based on information temperature.

    Semantic Chunking

    Attention bridges identify natural break points in code — preserves coherent logical units, not arbitrary line counts.

    MMR Deduplication

    Jaccard similarity across cached files — eliminates redundant patterns without losing unique information.

    BPE Optimization

    Token-aligned encoding — restructures output to minimize actual BPE token count, not just character count.

    Deep dive into all 6 algorithms

    Advanced Compression Pipeline

    Beyond basic compression, lean-ctx employs a multi-stage pipeline that adapts to each file and session context:

    Component What it does
    Thompson Sampling Bandit Adaptive threshold selection — learns which compression level works best per file type using multi-armed bandit exploration
    Tree-sitter AST Pruning Language-aware AST pruning — removes function bodies, comments, and boilerplate while preserving API signatures and type information
    IDF Deduplication Cross-file deduplication — identifies and removes content already seen in the session using inverse document frequency weighting
    Information-Bottleneck Filter Task-aware filtering — uses the Information Bottleneck principle to keep only content relevant to the current task context
    Verbatim Compaction Pattern-based compaction — collapses repetitive structures (repeated imports, similar log lines, boilerplate blocks) into counted summaries

    Noise, not signal

    Does compression hurt quality?

    No. lean-ctx uses AST parsing to understand code structure, then strips only what the LLM doesn't need: redundant whitespace, boilerplate imports, decorative comments. The signal stays intact.

    98% AST structure preserved on average — functions, classes, types, and their relationships stay intact
    97% identifiers preserved on average — function names, variable names, type annotations, import paths
    96% meaningful code lines retained on average — only boilerplate, comments, and low-entropy patterns removed
    Verify it yourself

    Run lean-ctx benchmark run in any project. It measures exact token savings and accuracy across every file in your codebase.

    Defense in depth

    Security Layer

    lean-ctx enforces a defense-in-depth security model to prevent LLM prompt injection from accessing files outside the project:

    • PathJail — All file operations are sandboxed to the project root. Symlink traversal, ../ escapes, and absolute paths outside the jail are blocked at the resolve_path chokepoint.
    • Bounded Shell Capture — Shell output is capped at 200KB with clear truncation markers. Prevents memory exhaustion from runaway commands.
    • TOCTOU Prevention — File edits use same file handle for read-verify-write, eliminating time-of-check-to-time-of-use race conditions.
    • Build Integrity — Compile-time integrity seed and hash verification detect tampered binaries. Checked automatically by lean-ctx doctor.
